editions.summary: A shooting at a Fairfield Halloween store left one dead and six hurt, and a new analysis challenges the federal list of “likely noncitizen” voters in California ahead of Tuesday’s election. Clocks fall back an hour this weekend. The Golden State Valkyries won their first WNBA title and will parade in San Francisco on Wednesday, the Warriors rest Stephen Curry against the Clippers, and NASA is asking industry how to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope.

headlines.title: Gunfire at a Fairfield Halloween store leaves one dead and six hurt
Analysis: 42% of names on DOJ’s “likely noncitizen” list aren’t on California’s voter rolls
Valkyries win the WNBA title in Game 7 for the franchise’s first championship
Netflix renews “The Diplomat” for a fifth season
NASA asks industry how to lift Hubble into a safer orbit

editions.summary: Job cuts kept coming as October ended, including small rounds at Dropbox and Front in San Francisco. Tech companies are now among the biggest outside spenders in California’s legislative races. The Warriors evened their record with a win over the Lakers, and tonight’s sky offers Saturn and early Halloween fireballs.

headlines.title: Layoffs pile up as October ends, including cuts in San Francisco
Tech money makes up at least a fifth of outside spending in California legislative races
Warriors beat the Lakers 112–95 to reach .500
Halloween night sky: Saturn and early fireballs

editions.summary: High tides and light rain could greet Bay Area trick-or-treaters this weekend, with a coastal flood advisory along the bay through Sunday. A CalMatters analysis finds Prop. 45 could open a door for data centers, and the Warriors host the Lakers tonight. Astronauts completed the 100th US spacewalk from the space station, and Virgin Galactic’s new space plane flew for the first time.

headlines.title: Halloween weekend brings a coastal flood advisory and a chance of drizzle
Could Prop. 45 open the door to more California data centers?
Astronauts mark the 100th US spacewalk from the space station
New this weekend: Apple TV’s Nocturne and Dexter: Resurrection season 2

editions.summary: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, but two officials wanted a hike. A federal judge refused to make California set aside 20,000 ballots, and the head of the state’s high-speed rail project resigned. San Mateo County voters weigh an $848 million college bond, Stephen Curry scored 44 in a Warriors win, and actor Patrick Stewart died at 86.

headlines.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75% to 4% as two officials push for a hike
Judge refuses to make California set aside 20,000 ballots
Measure V asks San Mateo County voters to extend an $848 million college bond
Patrick Stewart, Star Trek’s Captain Picard, dies at 86
Curry scores 44 as the Warriors win at Minnesota

editions.summary: A new investigation traces about $164 million that has flowed through San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie’s political and philanthropic network. In California, most of the state’s Republican House members have not signed a pledge to seat election winners. Astronomers may have found a sixth dwarf planet, GitHub launched a tool that picks AI models for you, and the final Dune: Part Three trailer arrived.

headlines.title: About $164 million has flowed through Mayor Lurie’s political and charity network
Most California Republicans in Congress skip a pledge to seat election winners
Astronomers spot a possible new dwarf planet beyond Neptune
Final Dune: Part Three trailer lands ahead of a Dec. 18 release

editions.summary: Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about a quarter of its workforce, and high tides flooded low-lying roads around the bay, with more expected this week. California’s ballot deadlines are closing in, and a river otter turned up on the San Mateo coast for the first time in more than a century. The Warriors got their first win, and Star Trek actor Walter Koenig died at 90.

headlines.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
King tides flood bayside roads, with more high water due this week
A river otter returns to the San Mateo coast after more than 100 years
Warriors earn their first win, routing Denver 134–114
Star Trek’s Walter Koenig, who played Chekov, dies at 90

editions.summary: San Mateo County is urging residents to get ready now for what could be a strong El Niño winter. The 49ers lost their first game of the season in Atlanta, and the Warriors try again for their first win tonight in Denver. Tonight’s Hunter’s Moon is the best full moon of the fall to catch rising.

headlines.title: San Mateo County urges early storm prep as a strong El Niño grows likely
49ers’ unbeaten run ends with a 29–20 loss in Atlanta
October’s Hunter’s Moon peaks overnight
New this week: The Mob on Hulu and Netflix’s Minimum Wage

editions.summary: The US pulled diplomats and their families from several Middle East posts after an intelligence warning about Iranian plots. Closer to home, seven more San Mateo County vote centers opened, and Californians are weighing about $44 billion in bond measures. The 49ers welcome back Christian Kirk for today’s game, Clayface led Friday’s box office, and the late-October sky offers a full moon and Halloween fireballs.

headlines.title: US pulls diplomats from Middle East posts after warning of Iranian plots
Seven more San Mateo County vote centers open ahead of Nov. 3
49ers activate Christian Kirk as Evans and Samuel sit out
California voters face about $44 billion in bond measures
Clayface leads Friday’s box office as a Nathan Fielder documentary expands

editions.summary: Bay Area voters are weighing a regional transit tax that decides the future of BART and Caltrain service, and San Francisco declared a local emergency to get ready for a wet El Niño winter. Abroad, burning tankers near the Strait of Hormuz kept US–Iran tensions high. The unbeaten 49ers head to Atlanta, DC’s Clayface opens in theaters, and NASA laid out a faster path back to the Moon.

headlines.title: Tankers burn near Hormuz as US–Iran tensions rise before the midterms
Bay Area transit tax on the Nov. 3 ballot would decide BART and Caltrain cuts
Unbeaten 49ers head to Atlanta short on healthy receivers
NASA lays out a faster Artemis plan aimed at a 2028 Moon landing
DC’s Clayface opens with $3.5 million in previews and strong reviews

editions.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom closed out his final bill-signing season with new limits on addictive social media features for teens, a child marriage ban and a slate of AI rules, while forecasters say Bay Area warmth could last into mid-October. Nationally, the Supreme Court let third-country deportations continue and the Pentagon confirmed the last U.S. troops have left Iraq. The unbeaten 49ers get ready for Denver, and SpaceX’s Crew-13 is set to launch this morning.

headlines.title: Newsom wraps up his last bill-signing season as governor
Supreme Court lets third-country deportations resume for now
Last U.S. troops leave Iraq, ending the anti-ISIS mission there
SpaceX Crew-13 set to launch to the space station this morning
Today in sports: unbeaten 49ers turn to Denver
